subject: FedAnalytics DPA: scope for no-training, derivative rights & cross-border subprocessors
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@fedanalytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: CSO Roberta Shaw <roberta.shaw@fedanalytics.com>, Legal Ops <legal@fedanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify DPA: use for model improvement and subprocessor transfers

Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile. Legal & procurement had a few open items on the DPA draft before we can move to signature. High level asks below so we can pull together our internal approval: 

1) No-training / no-model-improvement commitment: we need explicit language that FedAnalytics tenant data will not be used to further train or improve Redwood models, including derivatives used for future models. Please confirm how Redwood implements and enforces this at runtime and during model maintenance.
2) Output/derivative rights: confirm whether generated responses and any transformed artifacts are owned by FedAnalytics and whether there are any retention/export rights Redwood claims.
3) Subprocessors and transfers: we require a list of subprocessors that may have access to request data, and a process for notifying/approving any new subprocessor that may result in cross-border transfers.
4) Evidence & controls: SOC 2 report access, KMS location options (onshore), and a description of the audit trail for token-level access.

Could you send a redline or summary with the proposed clauses and an estimated timeline to resolve? We are aiming for countersignature by EOD Nov 17 if possible.

Attaching the draft DPA we returned with inline notes.

Thanks,
Maya Chen
FedAnalytics Procurement
procurement@fedanalytics.com

[Attachment: fedanalytics_dpa_v1.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@fedanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA: use for model improvement and subprocessor transfers

Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and a proposed next step. I'll get legal to redline the DPA and share our implementation notes.

1) No-training commitment: Redwood can commit that FedAnalytics customer input and responses will not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any general-purpose model. We support a tenant-level "no-learning" flag that prevents logging of training data and excludes requests from any model improvement pipelines.

2) Derivative/output rights: by default customers retain ownership of their outputs. We will add explicit language in the DPA stating FedAnalytics retains output rights and Redwood will not assert derivative IP claims for customer-generated content.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: attached is our current subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_overview.csv). We are happy to commit to 30-day notice for new subprocessors and an approval/objection workflow for cross-border transfers that materially affect data residency.

4) Evidence & controls: we can provide SOC 2 Type II summary, options for onshore KMS for encryption keys (additional charge/commitment for Dedicated/Private), and token-level audit records export. Dev has included a short tech note on how the no-train toggle is enforced.

Next steps: I attached a redlined DPA for your review (redwood_dpa_redline_FA.docx). Jonas — can you review the legal redline for any compliance gaps? Dev — can you confirm the KMS/onshore options and produce the no_train notes?

Schedule: we can aim to close redline by Wed Nov 11 and then circulate a countersigned DocuSign on Nov 13 to meet your Nov 17 target.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

[Attachments: redwood_dpa_redline_FA.docx, subprocessors_overview.csv]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fedanalytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA: use for model improvement and subprocessor transfers

Hi all — quick technical note to back up Kimberly's summary. Attached is an operations write-up. Highlights: 

- Runtime "no-learning" toggle: requests from an opt-out tenant are marked at ingress and routed through a path that disables logging to our training pipelines and excludes KV cache material from onboarding datasets.
- Ephemeral KV cache behavior: session-only KV is kept in memory and not persisted to long-term storage when no-learning is enabled.
- Onshore KMS: we support integrating customer key material into an onshore HSM/KMS for encryption-at-rest; for Hosted customers we offer a managed onshore key region via Dedicated offering or a contract amendment.
- Access logs & audit: token-level event streams can be exported to your secure S3 (or SFTP) on a daily cadence; we retain for 90 days by default but can extend per contract.

Known limitation: some advanced monitoring (large-scale usage aggregation for service health) uses anonymized telemetry that does not include tenant payloads but may include high-level token counts; we can add contractual guardrails around aggregation.

Let me know if you want a short run-through call to walk the engineering notes.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

[Attachment: no_train_implementation_notes.pdf]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@fedanalytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA: use for model improvement and subprocessor transfers

Maya / FedAnalytics team — I reviewed Kimberly's redline and added a few compliance-focused edits. Summary of proposed language below (see attached snippet):

- Explicit prohibition: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models used to provide Redwood services, including but not limited to derivative datasets, model weights, or prompts used for general model training."
- Confirmation of customer outputs: "Customer retains all rights to outputs and derivative works generated from Customer Data; Redwood waives any claim of ownership or license except as necessary to provide the service."
- Subprocessor process: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor inventory and agrees to notify Customer of any new subprocessor 30 days prior to onboarding; where a new subprocessor creates a cross-border transfer that materially affects residency, Redwood will allow Customer to object and seek remediation (technical or contractual).
- Evidence path: Redwood will make SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA and can provide KMS residency options for Dedicated/Private customers.

Operational notes: we recommend including a short SLA for evidence delivery (SOC 2 within 5 business days of request for red-team/trust review) and a documented remediation/rollback clause for unexpected subprocessor changes.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday Nov 12 10:00-10:30 PT to walk the redline? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Jonas Weber
Privacy & International Compliance
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

[Attachment: proposed_clause_snippet.txt]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@fedanalytics.com>, Legal Ops <legal@fedanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA: use for model improvement and subprocessor transfers

Maya — thanks for the fast turnaround and for flagging the timeline. Per our thread above, attached is the consolidated redline with specific clause language for the no-training commitment and subprocessor notification workflow. Key points we will include in the DPA: 

- Unambiguous no-train clause as Jonas proposed;
- Customer ownership of outputs and waiver of derivative claims by Redwood;
- 30-day notice for new subprocessors plus objection path for cross-border residency changes;
- SOC 2 Type II disclosure under NDA and KMS onshore options documented as an addendum (Dedicated/Private).

Action items
- Kimberly (me): send the final DocuSign via the link below to your Legal Ops once you confirm the redline is agreeable. (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/DocuSignLinkFA-2026-088)
- Procurement (Maya): confirm whether the 30-day notice plus objection right is acceptable or if you require a prior-approval model for certain regions.
- Dev: provide a brief run-through of the no_train_implementation_notes on our call if requested.

If we get sign-off, I'll route countersignature by Nov 16 so you can meet your internal deadline. Happy to hop on a call if you'd prefer to resolve the remaining points synchronously — I'm available Thursday afternoon.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
